invariants.text: Deny by default: an action is allowed only when a rule in this model allows it; missing data, missing context, or evaluation errors deny.
Every request is evaluated inside exactly one workspace tenant context, except explicitly privileged platform operations that run under a separate identity and iterate workspaces explicitly.
Tenant isolation is evaluated first and cannot be granted, shared, elevated, or overridden by any role, grant, or support process.
Access is never inferred from IDs, URLs, relationships, mentions, notifications, search indexes, cached projections, or ownership labels.
Relationships and associations never grant access; containment inherits only scope grants (brand/project) and never share grants.
The all-brands view aggregates authorized records and owns no data.
Inaccessible records, brands, relationships, counts, types, snippets, derived conditions, and related metadata are omitted; not-found and not-authorized are indistinguishable.
Authorization is applied before data contributes to counts, sorting, pagination, calculations, recommendations, AI context, exports, notifications, or webhooks.
Client-side permission checks are presentation only; the server re-evaluates every request and never trusts client-supplied workspace, brand, role, plan, approval, or actor fields.
Ownership (record owner, connection owner) is a responsibility field, not an access grant.
No principal can grant, share, delegate, or configure authority beyond its own grantable authority.

Revocation takes effect on the next authorization check everywhere: sessions, caches, live streams, jobs, agent tool calls, tokens, and external access paths. In-flight external effects are cancelled when safely possible; already-sent content cannot be recalled and is recorded as such.
Plan entitlements can only remove capabilities; they never grant data access.

Execution layers (AI, agents, automations, integrations, tokens, jobs) never have a broader read or write path than the delegating principal and their explicit scope; access can only shrink during execution.
Agents, automations, integrations, and AI can never approve, accept, verify, or decide; only authorized humans can.
Secrets are never readable after storage and never appear in records, permission data, logs, errors, exports, prompts, search, or audit display.
Every material permission change, elevation, support access, and denied high-risk attempt produces an immutable audit or security event.
Field-level restrictions propagate to every derived output: filters, sorts, formulas, conflicts, history, activity, notifications, search, exports, AI.

principals.description: Authenticated person (identity). Holds no tenant rights by itself; selects one membership per request.
Active non-guest workspace membership (owner, administrator, member, limited member, read-only roles).
Guest membership: access only to records explicitly shared with it.
Group of memberships; holds grants, never acts.
Platform staff identity from a separate identity provider; no tenant access without a customer-granted, time-boxed support access grant or audited break-glass.
Token acting as its creator: creator's current access ∩ token scopes.
Workspace service identity with explicit grants and an accountable owner; used by service API tokens.
External assistant or MCP client acting for a consenting user: user's current access ∩ consented scopes ∩ client registration scopes.
Connection identity for sync: mapped brand/project scopes ∩ provider scopes ∩ connection owner's current authority for outbound disclosure.
Signature-authenticated endpoint limited to one configured intake action into one configured scope; no read access.
Automation definition's service principal: declared scope and action set ∩ accountable owner's current authority ∩ trigger record scope.
AI action on behalf of a human: initiating human's current access ∩ explicitly selected context; no grants of its own.
Agent identity with explicit scope grants and tool-class grants.
Run scope = profile grants ∩ assigner access ∩ assignment scope at start, re-evaluated on every tool call (can only shrink).
One tool call: run scope ∩ tool class grant ∩ approval state of its action class.
Background job with a durable workspace and effective-principal context; system jobs hold only their job kind's allow-listed capabilities.
Public unauthenticated link visitor. Disabled by default; future capability requiring a separate threat model and OD-27 approval.

roles.description: Implicit manage on all non-sensitive brands and workspace scope; all administrative capabilities; only role for non-delegable actions. Sensitive brands/restricted projects need explicit grants or audited elevation.
Implicit manage on non-sensitive brands; workspace administration except billing ownership, deletion, ownership transfer, retention, legal hold.
No implicit brand access; brand/project access via scope grants; workspace-scoped records at the workspace default level (view).
Internal user with no implicit workspace or brand access; only explicit brand/project/record grants; reduced administrative abilities.
All access capped at view; no comments, edits, or execution beyond policy-enabled read-only AI.
External user; only explicitly shared records at the share level (≤ edit); no scope grants, directory, aggregation, trash, or onward sharing.

risk_classes.meaning: Informational or trivially reversible internal action
External disclosure, financial, access-changing, or integration effect
risk_classes.default_controls: confirmation + step-up where flagged; agents/automations need human approval or a pre-approved standing grant

risk_classes.meaning: Irreversible, production, security, ownership, or legal effect
risk_classes.default_controls: step-up; independent approver when policy enabled and available; never automatable

approval_classes.meaning: An approver other than the requester when another approval-capable human exists; otherwise labelled self-approval if policy allows.
For agent tool classes: a human approval per action instance.
For agent tool classes: changes held for human review before taking effect.
For agent tool classes: allowed without per-action review when workspace low-impact policy enables it (OD-23).

agent_tool_classes.description: Read authorized records within run scope.
Create subtasks under the run's own task.
Attach artifacts/deliverable versions to the run's task.
Update fields of records in scope.
Trigger test runs in non-production environments.
Push branches or open pull requests in mapped repositories.
Send messages outside the product (email, chat, issue comments).
Incur cost beyond the run's reserved budget or purchase.
Change permissions, shares, tokens, or memberships.
Trash, purge, overwrite, or delete data.
Deploy, migrate, or change production systems.
Read or act outside the snapshot scope (always requires a new approved assignment).

actions.description: Read a record and its own comments/attachments.
Create a record in a container.
Edit fields of a record.
Archive a record and its contained subtree.
Restore from archive or trash using current effective permission.
Move a record (and batch) to trash.
Irreversibly delete a trash batch before its scheduled purge.
actions.notes: Requires trash.manage authority over the scope; independent approver when policy enabled.

actions.description: Comment, reply, react, mention in comments.
Edit or delete own comment (revision retained per OD-38).
Delete another person's comment.
Follow or unfollow a readable record.
Assign or reassign people (only people who can read the record).
Delegate own assigned work to another eligible person.
Create a dependency/related link; requires edit on source and view on target.
Attach files or links to a record.
Download a file version (clean scan state only).
Move within a brand (change container); needs edit on source and destination.
Move a subtree to another brand (ownership change).
actions.notes: Manage on source and create (edit) on target brand. Tasks (2B, AZ-22): manage in both brands, with an exposure preview and confirmation.

actions.description: Create or change an explicit record grant (share) to a brand, member, team, or guest.
actions.notes: Share level ≤ sharer's level; never onward-sharable; restricted projects disallow record shares unless the project allows them.

actions.description: Revoke a share (the original sharer or a manager).
Export records or the current filtered view (permission-filtered).
Move a task to a done-category status; completion gates apply.
Complete a task whose required criteria or descendants are incomplete, recording a reason (ADR-22).
actions.notes: Human principals only; the reason and the visible incomplete count are audited (AZ-22). Never satisfied by a share.

actions.description: Create, rename, reorder, archive, and restore a brand's labels (OD-10).
actions.notes: Labels never grant authority (AZ-22).

actions.description: Complete a project (human decision).
Verify a project update as an accountable human (OD-16).
actions.notes: Human principals only; authoring never verifies; AI, imported, and system drafts stay unverified until this action (AZ-21).

actions.description: Define, pause, or resume a project recurrence, or generate its next occurrence (OD-14).
actions.notes: Each generated occurrence also requires record.create in the project's brand, rechecked by the worker before each step (AZ-21).

actions.description: Submit a deliverable version for review.
Request a review or approval.
Approve/accept, request changes, or reject as an eligible reviewer; evaluated at decision time.
actions.notes: Reviewer must be designated by the reviewer rule, be human, and be able to read the whole subject scope (UXD-11).

actions.description: Decide a review on one's own submission.
actions.notes: Default on only while exactly one approval-capable human exists; always labelled and audited (OD-20).

actions.description: Record a manual verification of a defect fix.
actions.notes: Verifier must not be the fixer when policy requires independence.

actions.description: Create/edit own time entries and timers on readable work.
Submit own timesheet.
Approve a timesheet's brand line.
Unlock an approved period with reason.
Share a saved view, dashboard, or report to a scope (never grants record access).
Schedule report delivery to recipients (rendered per recipient).
Record a go/no-go decision as an eligible approver.
Trigger or record a production deployment or rollback.
Configure environments and their URLs/evidence.
Start or rerun test runs.
Inbox, Today, notifications, personal views, favorites, reminders, availability, profile.
List and revoke own sessions.
Enroll an authenticator (TOTP) factor on own account.
actions.notes: Account-level (platform scope, no workspace or membership): 'own' means the authenticated account's own factors only; it is never a tenant capability. Human-only and not delegable to tokens, agents, automations, integrations, or support: step-up is human-only (0D §11.2) and no 0D scope may list this action. Step-up accepts the password when no factor exists yet, so enrollment never requires MFA before the first MFA.

actions.description: Turn off own two-step verification and remove its factor and recovery codes.
actions.notes: Account-level (platform scope, no workspace or membership): 'own' means the authenticated account's own factors only; it is never a tenant capability. Human-only and not delegable to tokens, agents, automations, integrations, or support: step-up is human-only (0D §11.2) and no 0D scope may list this action.

actions.description: Replace own recovery codes; the previous set stops working immediately.
actions.notes: Account-level (platform scope, no workspace or membership): 'own' means the authenticated account's own factors only; it is never a tenant capability. Human-only and not delegable to tokens, agents, automations, integrations, or support: step-up is human-only (0D §11.2) and no 0D scope may list this action.

actions.description: Create, rotate, revoke own personal API tokens (write scopes need step-up).
actions.notes: Read-only role may only create read scopes.

actions.description: Create a workspace and become its bootstrap owner (verified human account, before any tenant context exists).
actions.notes: Account-level platform command (AZ-18), listed in account_commands. No workspace role cell grants it: no membership exists before the workspace, so every cell is deny and holding any role never confers it. Only the authenticated human account principal may exercise it; tokens, service principals, OAuth clients, integrations, automations, AI, agents, support, and system jobs cannot, and no 0D scope may list it. Gates: verified email, active (not deleted) account, per-account rate limit, Idempotency-Key. It creates authority only by atomically creating the canonical workspace, the active owner membership, and the bootstrap owner assignment.

actions.description: View workspace name, locale, timezone, currency, week start.
Edit workspace profile and defaults.
Request workspace deletion.
Transfer workspace ownership (last-owner protection).
Create a brand.
Edit brand identity, settings, calendars, goals, notification rules, AI profile.
Archive or restore a brand.
Trash a brand.
Mark or unmark a brand sensitive (removes implicit role access).
Invite members (role ≤ inviter's grantable roles).
Invite a guest by sharing a record with an email.
actions.notes: Also requires record.share on each record shared.

actions.description: Change workspace roles, suspend, or remove memberships (owners managed only by owners).
Accept a workspace invitation addressed to the authenticated account's verified email.
actions.notes: Account command (AZ-19): performed before any membership exists, so every workspace role cell is deny. Only the human account principal may exercise it and no 0D scope may list it. Gates: verified email equal to the invitation's normalized email, active account, single-use unexpired token, per-account rate limit, Idempotency-Key. It creates authority only by atomically activating the membership and exactly the role assignment or record grants the invitation proposed.

actions.description: Accept an ownership transfer addressed to one's own active internal membership.
actions.notes: Recipient side of ownership.transfer (AZ-19): 'own' means only a pending transfer addressed to the caller's own membership. Human-only (step-up); never delegable to tokens, agents, automations, or integrations, and no 0D scope may list it. Guests can never become owners.

actions.description: Leave a workspace (end one's own membership).
actions.notes: Own membership only. Refused while the caller is the last active owner or while registered owned resources cannot be reassigned or suspended (AZ-19). Human-only; no 0D scope may list it.

actions.description: Create teams and change team membership (actor needs authority over every scope the team holds grants in).
Assign scope roles (access levels) at workspace, brand, or project.
Mark a project/document restricted or set field visibility.
Preview a principal's effective permissions within scopes the previewer manages.
Break-glass: owner grants themselves access to a sensitive brand or restricted project with reason; notifies scope managers.
Configure sharing, guest, export, self-approval, and public-link policy.
Configure feature availability by role.
Create custom roles from allowed capabilities.
Configure workflows, statuses, transitions, required fields, and approval policies.
actions.notes: Phase 2C (AZ-23): at the workflow's own scope (workspace, brand, or project), within grantable authority; no owner/admin bypass on sensitive brands or restricted projects.

actions.description: Configure custom fields and field sets.
actions.notes: Phase 2C (AZ-23): definitions, options, formulas, field policies, and field sets at their own scope.

actions.description: Set default views per brand/project and pin shared views to navigation.
Create and manage templates.
Configure brand/project notification rules and minimal-content mode.
Configure brand AI profile and approved-source policy.
Configure AI providers, models, workspace keys, data settings.
Configure AI/agent/automation allowances and hard caps.
Create agent profiles; grant scopes and tool classes (within grantor authority).
Create/enable automations within the configurer's authority.
Connect, map, reauthorize, disconnect integrations.
Create and manage service principals and their tokens.
Manage outbound webhooks and inbound endpoints.
MFA requirements, session policy, allowed sign-in methods.
Revoke other members' sessions and tokens.
Configure retention parameters (values pending OD-34/36).
Place or release legal holds (extension point, OD-37).
Inspect and restore any trash batch within authorized scope.
View audit history (field values redacted per viewer).
Export audit history.
Full workspace export.
View usage and cost (brand-level for brand managers).
View plan, entitlements, invoices.
Change plan, seats, payment method; approve extra usage purchases.
See that credentials exist, scopes, last rotation (never values).
View integration, automation, and agent health.
Grant platform support time-boxed, scoped access.
Stop all agent execution in the workspace.
actions.notes: Never blocked by approval; resuming requires owner/admin.

actions.description: Run an AI action over a selected readable context.
Apply selected AI-proposed changes (each change authorized as the applying human).
Assign a task to an agent and start runs.
Pause, resume, cancel, or retry a run (assigner or task manager).
Approve a gated agent action class (external message, publish, spend, access, destructive, production, scope expansion).
Run or test an automation manually.
Trigger a sync on a connection.
Run an import into a scope.
Send a test delivery to an outbound webhook.
Preview and apply a workflow status transition (including Complete, Cancel, and Reopen).
actions.notes: Phase 2C (AZ-23). Preview and apply share one evaluator; a generic edit that changes status is evaluated the same way.

actions.description: Request approval for a gated transition.
actions.notes: Phase 2C (AZ-23). The request is bound to the record version; any change makes it stale.

actions.description: Approve or reject a pending transition approval.
actions.notes: Phase 2C (AZ-23). Also requires eligibility by the transition policy: manage on the record (one_manager) or being a named approver (all_named_approvers). Being an approver grants no access. Self-approval needs both the transition flag and the workspace self_approval policy (OD-20). Human principals only.

actions.description: Read custom field values on a record, subject to field policy.
actions.notes: Phase 2C (AZ-23). Intersected with access.field_policy and definition applicability; hidden fields are absent everywhere (0C §7.2).

actions.description: Edit custom field values on a record, subject to field policy.
actions.notes: Phase 2C (AZ-23). Formula results are never editable. Person and label values grant no access.

actions.description: Inspect a formula's inputs, dependencies, and error on a record.
actions.notes: Phase 2C (AZ-23). Only when every input is readable; never reveals hidden input values or names.

actions.description: Set, change, or dismiss one's own reminder on a readable task.
actions.notes: Phase 2D (AZ-24): personal; grants nothing and changes nothing on the task. The worker rechecks record.read before firing; a reminder whose task became unreadable is cancelled silently.

actions.description: Snooze or unsnooze a readable task for oneself.
actions.notes: Phase 2D (AZ-24): personal; never edits dates, status, or access, and is invisible to others.

actions.description: Define, pause, resume, or end a task recurrence, or generate its next occurrence.
actions.notes: Phase 2D (AZ-24): each occurrence also requires record.create in the series' brand (and project), rechecked by the worker before each step; a series whose owner lost it pauses.

account_commands.grants: bootstrap owner (workspace role owner) to the creating account's new membership only
exactly the role assignment (internal) or record grants (guest) the invitation proposed
